prompts: If I decorate my Python function with @weave.op, will that alone give me the new Agents view with conversations and turns?

output.answer:
The docs I found don't say that `@weave.op` alone populates the Agents view. They describe a separate path for it.

- **`@weave.op` traces Ops, not agent conversations.** The Agents tracing guide says that if you trace individual functions as Ops with `@weave.op`, you should read "Trace LLM applications" instead [S1]. `@weave.op` tracks a function as a Call and captures its inputs and outputs [S6]. I found nothing in the searched snapshot saying that it creates conversations or turns.

- **The Agents view is built from agent-specific spans.** The Weave SDK for Agents models conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool executions. Each of these emits an OpenTelemetry span tagged with attributes such as `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id` [S1].

**How to get conversations and turns in the Agents view**

1. **Use a built-in integration.** For a supported agent harness or agent SDK, you install a plugin or call `weave.init()`, and Weave autopatches the framework [S2].
   - Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own [S2].
   - Agent SDKs run one turn per call, so your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation. For these, `weave.init()` alone isn't enough [S2].

2. **Instrument it yourself with the Weave agent tracing APIs.**
   - `weave.start_conversation()` stamps a `conversation_id` on child spans so turns are grouped. Reuse the same ID to add turns to an existing conversation [S4].
   - `weave.start_turn()` creates an `invoke_agent` span that represents one user-agent exchange. If no conversation is active, the turn has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped with other turns [S5].
   - The guide also covers LLM calls and tool calls. I only read the conversation and turn sections in detail.

Once you instrument your agent this way and run it, the traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. The Conversations tab lists conversations, and the detail view shows turns, LLM calls and tool executions [S7].

**Limits of this answer:** I didn't find a page that explicitly says `@weave.op` can never feed the Agents view. I'm relying on the documented requirements above. Which path fits you depends on whether you use a supported harness or SDK or a custom agent. If you tell me which, I can narrow this down.

sources.heading: Trace your agents
sources.text:
# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

# Choose an agent integration

> Pick a built-in Weave integration for your agent SDK or harness and start sending conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls to the Agents view.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/get-started/integrations.md).

W\&B Weave traces multi-turn agents built with popular SDKs and harnesses without hand-instrumenting each turn. Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK, and Weave autopatches the framework. Conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls render in the **Agents** view of your project.

Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own, because the harness owns the session. Agent SDKs run one turn per call, so your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation. For those integrations, `weave.init()` alone isn't enough.

Choose from one of the following supported integrations.

## How data appears in the Weights & Biases UI

After you instrument your agent with the preceding patterns and run it, your traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project at `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]/weave/agents`.

* The **Conversations tab** shows all conversations with a minimap of turn activity.
* The **Conversation detail view** opens when you click a conversation and shows all turns, its LLM calls, tool executions, token counts, and any attached feedback.

For details on viewing Agents data in Weave, see [View agent activity](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md).

results.title: Bedrock Agents
results.heading: Multi-turn conversations
results.snippet:
## Multi-turn conversations

Bedrock Agents preserve conversation state on the service side when you reuse a `sessionId`. To group multiple turns into a single trace in the Weights & Biases UI, wrap the turns in `weave.thread`:

```python lines theme={"system"}
with weave.thread("support-conversation") as t:
    for prompt in [
        "I can't log in to my account.",
        "I already tried resetting my password.",
    ]:
        ask_agent(prompt, session_id=t.thread_id)
```

Weave displays each turn in the UI as individual rows in the Threads view.

results.heading: Get started
results.snippet:
## Get started

To open the Agents view for your project:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.
2. In the sidebar menu, select **Agents** to view all agent conversations saved for your project.

The Agents view is organized into a row of tabs across the top: **Dashboard**, **Agents**, **Conversations**, **Spans**, and **Signals**. The **Dashboard** tab gives a project-wide overview of agent activity, while the other tabs let you drill into individual agents, conversations, spans, and signals.

results.snippet:
## Track custom functions

LLM applications often have additional logic, such as pre-processing and post-processing, prompts, and more, that you want to track. Use this approach when you want Weave to capture your own functions alongside the LLM calls it traces automatically.

**Python**

Weave lets you manually track these Calls using the [`@weave.op`](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/reference/python-sdk#function-op) decorator. For example:

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave

# Initialize Weave Tracing
weave.init('intro-example')

# Decorate your function
@weave.op
def my_function(name: str):
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

# Call your function -- Weave will automatically track inputs and outputs
print(my_function("World"))
```

You can also track [methods on classes](#track-class-and-object-methods).

**TypeScript**

Weave lets you manually track these Calls by wrapping your function with [`weave.op`](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/reference/typescript-sdk/functions/op). For example:

sources.text:
# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

# Choose an agent integration

> Pick a built-in Weave integration for your agent SDK or harness and start sending conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls to the Agents view.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/get-started/integrations.md).

W\&B Weave traces multi-turn agents built with popular SDKs and harnesses without hand-instrumenting each turn. Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK, and Weave autopatches the framework. Conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls render in the **Agents** view of your project.

Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own, because the harness owns the session. Agent SDKs run one turn per call, so your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation. For those integrations, `weave.init()` alone isn't enough.

Choose from one of the following supported integrations.

## How data appears in the Weights & Biases UI

After you instrument your agent with the preceding patterns and run it, your traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project at `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]/weave/agents`.

results.heading: Multi-turn conversations
results.snippet:
## Multi-turn conversations

Bedrock Agents preserve conversation state on the service side when you reuse a `sessionId`. To group multiple turns into a single trace in the Weights & Biases UI, wrap the turns in `weave.thread`:

```python lines theme={"system"}
with weave.thread("support-conversation") as t:
    for prompt in [
        "I can't log in to my account.",
        "I already tried resetting my password.",
    ]:
        ask_agent(prompt, session_id=t.thread_id)
```

Weave displays each turn in the UI as individual rows in the Threads view.

## Get started

To open the Agents view for your project:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.
2. In the sidebar menu, select **Agents** to view all agent conversations saved for your project.

The **Dashboard** tab gives a project-wide overview of agent activity, while the other tabs let you drill into individual agents, conversations, spans, and signals.

## Track custom functions

LLM applications often have additional logic, such as pre-processing and post-processing, prompts, and more, that you want to track. Use this approach when you want Weave to capture your own functions alongside the LLM calls it traces automatically.

**Python**

Weave lets you manually track these Calls using the [`@weave.op`](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/reference/python-sdk#function-op) decorator. For example:

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave

# Initialize Weave Tracing
weave.init('intro-example')

# Decorate your function
@weave.op
def my_function(name: str):
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

# Call your function -- Weave will automatically track inputs and outputs
print(my_function("World"))
```

You can also track [methods on classes](#track-class-and-object-methods).

**TypeScript**

Weave lets you manually track these Calls by wrapping your function with [`weave.op`](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/reference/typescript-sdk/functions/op). For example:

## How data appears in the Weights & Biases UI

After you instrument your agent with the preceding patterns and run it, your traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project at `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]/weave/agents`.

* The **Conversations tab** shows all conversations with a minimap of turn activity.
* The **Conversation detail view** opens when you click a conversation and shows all turns, its LLM calls, tool executions, token counts, and any attached feedback.

For details on viewing Agents data in Weave, see [View agent activity](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md).

"Trace your agents" points readers who trace functions with `@weave.op` to the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead. The answer also correctly says the Agents view is built from conversation, turn, LLM and tool spans tagged with GenAI attributes. It gives two valid routes. The first is the built-in integrations (S2), including the point that `weave.init()` alone isn't enough for agent SDKs. The second is manual instrumentation with `start_conversation()` and `start_turn()` (S4, S5). It describes the result in the UI correctly (S7). Every citation supports the claim it is attached to, and no APIs are invented.

Minor issues:
- For the do-it-yourself route, the answer never says that `weave.init()` must be called before `start_conversation()`/`start_turn()`, or that these functions silently do nothing without it ("Before you begin"). That is part of the expected initialization guidance.
